models_evaluated: 107 LLMs (reasoning, non-reasoning, medical, and general-purpose models)

links.outcome: Rate of stigmatizing terms in LLM-generated reasoning text across clinical tasks
links.effect: Stigma rates ranged from 0% to 33.33%; 84.06% of 3,745 model-task pairs contained stigma terms; 19.76% of pairs amplified stigma in input notes.
links.quote: Results showed that stigma rates ranged from 0% to 33.33%, with 84.06% of pairs containing stigma terms.

links.outcome: Change in stigma rate and model performance after destigmatizing prompt engineering
links.effect: Prompt engineering reduced stigma rates by up to 91.91% without compromising model performance, though effectiveness varied across models.
links.quote: The effectiveness of prompt engineering as a destigmatizing approach varied across models, with stigma rates reduced by up to 91.91% without compromising model performance.

unlisted_practices: Direct stigma-related safety evaluation of LLM outputs using a validated stigma-term NLP detector before clinical deployment

screen.reason: The study empirically assesses stigmatizing language across 107 LLMs on 35 clinical tasks and evaluates prompt engineering as a destigmatizing safeguard, showing up to a 91.91% reduction in stigma rates.
